title: Snake lemma for modules (Stacks 07JW)
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccccccc}X&\xrightarrow{f}&Y&\xrightarrow{g}&Z&\to&0\\ \downarrow\alpha&&\downarrow\beta&&\downarrow\gamma&&\\ U&\xrightarrow{k}&V&\xrightarrow{l}&W&&\end{array}$$
be a commutative diagram of $\Lambda$-modules and $\Lambda$-linear maps ($\beta f=k\alpha$, $\gamma g=l\beta$) whose rows are exact ($\ker g=\operatorname{im}f$, $g$ surjective, $k$ injective, $\ker l=\operatorname{im}k$). Then there is a $\Lambda$-linear map $\partial:\ker\gamma\to\operatorname{coker}\alpha$ (for $z\in\ker\gamma$ choose $y\in Y$ with $g(y)=z$ and $u\in U$ with $k(u)=\beta(y)$, and put $\partial z=u\bmod\operatorname{im}\alpha$; this is independent of the choices) such that the sequence
$$\ker\alpha\xrightarrow{f'}\ker\beta\xrightarrow{g'}\ker\gamma\xrightarrow{\ \partial\ }\operatorname{coker}\alpha\xrightarrow{k'}\operatorname{coker}\beta\xrightarrow{l'}\operatorname{coker}\gamma$$
is exact, where $f',g'$ are the restrictions of $f,g$ and $k',l'$ are induced by $k,l$. If moreover $l$ is surjective, then $l'$ is surjective; if $f$ is injective, then $f'$ is injective.
